This week, Apple launched a brand-new rental program called Apple Upgrade, covering the vast majority of Apple products. The program completely replaces the iPhone Upgrade Program and, overall, is an extremely good deal.

This deal is so good that there's basically no longer a strong reason to keep using Apple Card Monthly Installments (ACMI). You still get 3% back with Apple Upgrade, similar to ACMI, but the rental terms are far more flexible than ACMI—and you don't have to rent forever. When the rental term ends, you can choose to buy the device by simply paying the difference between what you've paid in rent and the original price.

So this leads me to wonder—will Apple Card Monthly Installments be discontinued?

Apple Card Transitioning to Chase

Earlier this year, Apple announced that Apple Card's partner bank would be switching from Goldman Sachs to JPMorgan Chase. The transition isn't scheduled to happen until early 2028, so there's still quite a long time before any changes take effect.

Although this isn't any kind of confirmation, the wording on Apple's Apple Card transition website doesn't seem entirely clear. Regarding the future of Apple Card Monthly Installments, the website says:

Apple uses wording like "will be able to continue," which doesn't inspire a great deal of confidence that the program will be around for long. Apple is only confirming that there won't be any changes in the short term.

Apple Upgrade

As I mentioned at the start, Apple Upgrade is an extremely good deal and essentially replaces the need to use Apple Card Monthly Installments. Apple Upgrade offers more flexibility, provides longer repayment terms, and you can still earn 3% back with Apple Card—and if you ultimately want to own the product, you can buy it outright without paying more than the original price.

That said, Apple Upgrade is launched in partnership with Klarna—which raises the question: why not Chase? Since Chase is going to be Apple Card's partner bank, why aren't they also powering this brand-new rental program for Apple?

Simply put, I don't think there's a huge profit margin in this business. After all, there's no interest on financing and no late fees—so the financial returns for a major bank are pretty limited. Goldman Sachs has already learned that the hard way.

If Chase isn't willing to power Apple Upgrade, they may not be willing to power ACMI either—so it wouldn't be all that surprising if that program eventually disappeared. Apple Upgrade has largely replaced it, with the only shortcoming being that a few products aren't included—but that can be adjusted later.

Of course, all of this is purely speculation—but the timing seems a little too obvious to me. I believe Apple Card Monthly Installments will continue to exist in the short term, but I wouldn't be at all surprised if Apple stops accepting new ACMI purchases at some point before 2028.
